core_meaning.short_meaning: Steadfast anchor, one who shelters; companion Wathilah ibn al-Asqa'.
core_meaning.primary_meaning: Wathilah (وَاثِلَة) is an Arabic masculine given name meaning 'one who connects steadfastly', 'firm foundation', or 'a reliable refuge'. In Islamic history, it is the renowned name of Wathilah ibn al-Asqa' al-Laythi, one of the prominent companions of Ahl al-Suffah who served the Prophet closely and narrated major prophetic hadiths.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: Derived from wathala (to be firm, rooted, or bonded), indicating stability, enduring allegiance, and trustworthy support.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: The root w-th-l in classical lexicons signifies staying firmly attached, rootedness, and a dependable refuge. Wathilah ibn al-Asqa' embraced Islam shortly before the expedition of Tabuk, dedicated himself to learning at the Prophet's mosque among Ahl al-Suffah, and became one of the long-lived companions whose teachings preserved authentic hadith across Syria and Palestine.
